newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols firm as spot extends gains.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols firm as spot extends gains.

text.p: Dollar/mark option volatilities were higher at midday Europe, pushed up by dollar spot's rise to its highest in nearly eight years.
Dollar/mark vols firmed on spot's poke above the 1.87 level, its first time since October 1989, already emboldened by spot's clearance on Friday of the key 1.85 marks level.

"The technical levels are just falling away and the outlook still points to a higher dollar and vols," said a U.S. bank dealer. "Dollar call buying is emerging above 2.00 marks in the one-year but trade is pretty sleepy and the moves choppy at the moment."

One-month dollar/mark volatility was trading at 10.6/10.9 percent against 10.3/10.7 percent late Friday. The risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility of calls relative to puts, increased their mark put bias to 0.6/0.8 from 0.3/0.6 on Friday.
Expectations that German growth is too weak to bear an interest rate rise plus evidence of strong U.S. economic growth has served to fuel the dollar gains, said dealers.

Dollar/yen spot, meantime, held below the key 119 level despite breaking briefly above here on Friday. But spot's failure to hold above this level has kept vols on the back burner and the one-month was little changed from late Friday at 11.4/11.7 percent.
The dollar/yen risk reversal was slightly firmer for yen puts at 0.3/0.6 from 0.2/0.5 late Friday.

Sterling/mark vols were also steady amid a firmer spot rate. Dealers said trade was cautious ahead of this week's Bank of England monetary policy meeting with some positioning ahead of what are expected to be fairly volatile conditions in coming days.
"The market is pretty evenly divided on whether we get a UK rate hike this week but the main risk is for steady rates and lower spot," said the U.S. bank dealer.
One-month vol stood at 10.6/10.9 percent against 10.5/10.9 percent on Friday. The one-month risk reversal remained around par.
Cable was slightly easier, pressured by dollar strength, and one-month volatility was also down slightly at 8.35/8.65 percent from 8.4/8.8 percent.
